lines.explanation: The payer denied manual therapy as not medically necessary (CO-50). The policy requires the note to state the body region treated and the clinical finding that supports manual therapy, and the note records only the minutes.

evidence.quote: Manual therapy (CPT 97140) requires documentation of the body region treated and the clinical finding that supports it, such as joint hypomobility or soft tissue restriction.

lines.next_steps: Do not appeal, because the record does not support overturning the denial. For future visits, the note for any 97140 should name the body region treated and the supporting finding, such as joint hypomobility or soft tissue restriction.

analysis.summary: Two lines totaling $203.00 billed were denied for medical necessity (CO-50). The $141.00 therapeutic exercise line looks recoverable by appeal: the plan of care has measurable goals, the 09/18 note shows measurable progress, and 40 documented minutes support 3 units. The $62.00 manual therapy line is not supported, because the note does not state the body region treated or a supporting clinical finding.

CLM-88310427.letter:
[PRACTICE NAME]
[DATE]

Health Plan Appeals Department

Re: Appeal of Medical Necessity Denial
Member ID: M-62018
Claim number: CLM-88310427
Payer claim number: 26261-004417
Date of service: 2026-09-18
Remit date: 2026-10-09

Appealed line:
Line 2: CPT 97110-GP x3, therapeutic exercise, billed $141.00, denied CO-50

Dear Appeals Department,

We are appealing the denial of Line 2 on the claim above. The service was denied under CO-50 as not medically necessary. The documentation meets the payer's own coverage criteria, so we ask that this line be reprocessed for payment.

Policy DEMO-PT-001, Outpatient physical therapy documentation, states: "Therapeutic exercise (CPT 97110) is medically necessary when a current plan of care documents measurable functional goals and the progress notes show measurable progress toward those goals."

Both conditions are met.

Measurable functional goals: The current plan of care, dated 2026-08-04, sets these goals: "1. Lift 25 lb from floor to waist without increase in pain, to return to warehouse work." and "3. Oswestry Disability Index below 20%."

Measurable progress: The progress note for the date of service documents: "Oswestry Disability Index 26% (42% at evaluation). Lifts 20 lb floor to waist with good mechanics and no pain increase. Sitting tolerance 45 minutes." The assessment states: "Assessment: Measurable progress on all three goals."

Units billed: The note records "Therapeutic exercise 40 minutes (lifting progression, core stabilization)." Policy DEMO-PT-001 allows "three units for 38 to 52 minutes," which supports the three units billed.

The plan of care and the progress note show that therapeutic exercise on 2026-09-18 met the criteria in Policy DEMO-PT-001. We respectfully request that Line 2, CPT 97110-GP x3, billed at $141.00, be overturned and paid.

Please contact our office with any questions.

Sincerely,

[PROVIDER NAME, CREDENTIALS]
[PRACTICE NAME]

CLM-87990314.letter:
[DATE]

Appeals Department

Re: Appeal of timely filing denial
Member ID: M-71442
Claim number: CLM-87990314
Payer claim number: 26273-002950
Original payer claim control number: 25203-114872
Date of service: 2025-07-14
Remittance date: 2026-10-16

To the Appeals Department:

[PRACTICE NAME] requests reconsideration of the following lines, both denied for timely filing:

Line 1: 99396, preventive visit, billed $245.00, denied CO-29
Line 2: 36415, routine venipuncture, billed $18.00, denied CO-29

The plan's timely filing policy, DEMO-ADM-010, states: "Claims must be received within 365 days of the date of service." For the 2025-07-14 date of service, that limit ended 2026-07-14. Claim 26273-002950 was resubmitted on 2026-09-30, after the limit. However, the original claim reached the plan well within the limit.

Our submission history shows the claim was sent on 2025-07-18. On 2025-07-22 it records: "277CA received from plan: claim accepted for adjudication. Payer claim control number 25203-114872." This acceptance date is inside the 365-day filing limit. On 2025-12-09, a status inquiry found that the plan had no claim on file under that control number. After follow-up, we resubmitted the claim, and it received the new number 26273-002950.

Policy DEMO-ADM-010 states: "The plan will reconsider a claim denied for timely filing when the provider submits proof that the original claim was received within the filing limit." It also states: "Acceptable proof is a claim acknowledgment (277CA) from the plan showing the payer claim control number and an acceptance date within the filing limit." The plan's 277CA acceptance of the original claim, dated 2025-07-22 under control number 25203-114872, is that proof. It shows the plan's own acceptance, not just a record that the claim was sent.

We ask the plan to reverse the CO-29 denials on lines 1 and 2 and process both lines for payment. Please contact our office if you need anything further.

Sincerely,

[PROVIDER NAME, CREDENTIALS]
[PRACTICE NAME]
